title: IDF, Shin Bet Announce Killing of Sinwar's Former Bodyguard and Second Nukhba Terrorist Who Infiltrated Re'im on Oct. 7
detail: The IDF and Shin Bet announced Thursday, August 27, 2026 that they had killed Razek Sahil Suleiman Abu Shahma, a Hamas Nukhba Force terrorist who served as a bodyguard to slain Hamas leader Yahya Sinwar and infiltrated the Re'im military base during the October 7, 2023 attack, along with a second Nukhba terrorist, Hazem Mousa, who also infiltrated Re'im that day. Both men were struck in the Khan Yunis area of southern Gaza earlier in the week. The military said both had continued advancing terror attacks against IDF troops and Israeli civilians and were working to rebuild Hamas's military capabilities in systematic violation of the ceasefire, and that precise munitions and aerial surveillance were used prior to the strike to mitigate harm to civilians. The killings are the latest in the IDF-Shin Bet 'Nili' campaign, which has now killed roughly 2,800 people on its target list of October 7 participants, according to officials cited in recent reporting on the campaign.

title: US Debars First UN-Agency-Linked Hamas Operative, Confirms Oct. 7 Body-Dragger Al-Naami Was Active Hamas Militant
detail: The USAID Office of Inspector General and US State Department announced this week that Hafez Mousa Mohammed Mousa, a former UNRWA school principal and Hamas East Jabaliya Battalion operative who coordinated communications with other Hamas members during the October 7, 2023 attack, has been formally debarred from US-funded foreign assistance programs — the first known US debarment of a terrorist affiliated with a UN humanitarian agency. Three additional former UNRWA teachers were proposed for debarment: a Hamas Deir al-Balah Battalion operative accused of helping abduct hostages on October 7, a Palestinian Islamic Jihad Rafah Brigade operative accused of infiltrating Israel that day, and a second Deir al-Balah Battalion operative accused of holding civilians hostage in Gaza. A USAID OIG spokesperson said its 'active and ongoing investigations help prevent terrorists from circulating across US-funded foreign assistance programs in Gaza.' Separately, investigative reporting by the Washington Free Beacon, citing USAID OIG findings, confirmed that Faisal Ali Al-Naami — an UNRWA-employed 'social worker' filmed on October 7 dragging the body of 21-year-old Yonatan Samerano into an SUV at Kibbutz Be'eri before it was taken into Gaza — was an active Hamas military-communications operative; USAID had considered proposing him for debarment but the case was dropped after he was confirmed killed in an Israeli strike in October 2023. A State Department official called the finding linking Al-Naami to the killing 'a game-changer,' and a department spokesman reiterated that no State Department funding will go to UNRWA. The referrals bring the total number of current or former UNRWA staff flagged by USAID OIG for October 7 participation or Hamas/Islamic Jihad affiliation since 2024 above 100, with further criminal referrals to the Department of Justice possible.
